title: Airline to Charge Passengers to Use Overhead Lockers
paragraphs: Finding space for a bag in the overhead lockers is often one of the most stressful parts of boarding a plane. Now, the Australian budget airline Jetstar has announced that it will start charging passengers to use them.

Under the new system, which will begin in February 2027, passengers who want to put a larger carry-on bag in the overhead lockers will have to pay for an option called "Priority Carry-on." The fee will cost between 25 and 52 Australian dollars per one-way flight, depending on the route. Passengers who buy this option will also be able to board the plane early, and their bags can weigh up to 10 kilograms, rather than the current 7 kilograms. In addition, staff will no longer weigh bags before boarding.
However, passengers will still be able to bring one smaller item, such as a handbag, laptop bag or backpack, for free, as long as it fits under the seat in front of them.

According to Jetstar, which is owned by Qantas, feedback from passengers and staff showed that checking bags at the gate and competing for overhead space were sources of stress. The airline says the change will reduce delays and speed up boarding. Its CEO, Stephanie Tully, said, "You only pay for what you need — traveling with less means paying less."

However, not everyone is happy. Bridget McKenzie, an opposition politician, called the fee a "cash grab" on social media. Meanwhile, Transport Minister Catherine King said that airlines should clearly show extra fees when customers are booking. "Jetstar claim this change is to keep fares affordable. It will be up to them to demonstrate that to passengers," she said.

Jetstar is not the first airline to introduce such a charge. Many low-cost airlines in the United States and Europe already charge passengers for bringing larger bags into the cabin. At the same time, several major American airlines raised their fees for checked bags in 2026, partly because of rising fuel prices.
